rules.rationale: Ionic halides lacking partly filled d states have the widest gaps; large electronegativity contrast maximizes valence-conduction separation.
Main-group oxides are insulators: deep O 2p valence bands and empty cation s conduction states give wide gaps.
Partially filled d manifolds insert low-lying conduction states, systematically shrinking measured optical gaps.
Counter-hypothesis: the metalloid source effect rests on 30 samples, so its Moss-inverted penalty is strongly downweighted here.

skill.hypothesis: Ionicity and closed-shell cation chemistry, not transferred dielectric magnitudes, drive experimental gaps; thin source relations are downweighted. May fail for lanthanide f-state compounds or defect-narrowed halide reports.
